title: An Icelandic pangenome reference.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC (via paper_context.py): not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links to GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP, and no Zenodo/Dryad record for the DOI. The nature.com article page redirects to a login (not read). I listed the DecodeGenetics GitHub repos and read the Emblask and weaver READMEs: both are code only (weaver is MIT-licensed), with small test files and no download link for the 698 Icelandic haplotypes, the HPRC-ICE graph (HPRC-ICE = the HPRC pangenome plus the Icelandic haplotypes) or variant calls.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract: 698 Icelandic haplotypes, 51.41 million small variants in HPRC-ICE, 57,630 Icelanders remapped, 98.96 million variants called, a GBA1 Parkinson's association replicated in UK Biobank (429,193 participants). I did not see the data availability statement. deCODE's individual-level Icelandic data is normally not shared under Icelandic law, and UK Biobank requires an application.

a1_downloadable.note: I found no public download for the Icelandic assemblies, graph or per-person variant calls. Only code is on GitHub. Individual-level deCODE data and UK Biobank both need an access application or are not shared at all. Checked through Europe PMC, NCBI links and GitHub; I could not read the paper's data statement because nature.com redirected to a login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: This is a methods/resource paper, a reference genome built from many individual genomes plus mapping software. There is no outcome column. A phenotype label (e.g. Parkinson's status) would have to come from controlled deCODE/UK Biobank records.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; no data files were available.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable; no tabular data was found.

a5_enough_rows.note: 57,630 genomes per the abstract, but none are public. I could not count any rows.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Remapping 57,630 short-read genomes to a pangenome graph is cluster-scale work.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible; the public output is software (Emblask, weaver) and summary statistics, not a labelled dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the genetic variants found only by mapping to the pangenome to predict which ones a standard linear reference genome misses.
plain_idea.train_on: Variant sites with their local genome context, labelled by whether a standard single reference genome missed them. The number is unknown because no public variant table was found.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a variant is detectable only with the pangenome, judged by comparing deCODE's own calls on the pangenome against calls on the linear reference.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show sequencing groups which genome regions need pangenome mapping. But the comparison table is not public, and the label is the output of two variant-calling pipelines rather than a lab measurement.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed because the project failed Part A.

ml_idea: None viable. The only data-like output would be pangenome-only versus linear-reference variant calls. That table is not public, and its labels come from pipelines, not measurements.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find a public download of HPRC-ICE variant sites or allele frequencies; none was found in Europe PMC, NCBI or deCODE's GitHub.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A2. The Icelandic genome data and UK Biobank are not public or need an access application; only the software is open, and there is no measured label column. The paper is also paywalled, so I could not read its data statement.
